fields.name: CCCRx
fields.raw: CCCR Format Version number. These 4 bits contain the version of the CCCR and FBR format that this card supports. Any change to the CCCR and/or the FBR structure shall cause a new version code to be assigned. The codes for the CCCR/FBR formats are as follows: Value CCCR/FBR Format Version 00h CCCR/FBR defined in SDIO Version 1.00 01h CCCR/FBR defined in SDIO Version 1.10 02h CCCR/FBR defined in SDIO Version 2.00 03h CCCR/FBR defined in SDIO Version 3.00 04h-0Fh Reserved for Future Use Addr: Field Type Description
fields.abstract: A read-only 4-bit field indicating the CCCR/FBR format version supported by the card, with values 00h-03h corresponding to SDIO specification versions 1.00 through 3.00.

fields.name: SDIOx
fields.raw: SDIO Specification Revision Number These 4 bits contain the version of the SDIO Specification that this card supports. The codes for the SDIO Specifications are as follows: Value SDIO Specification 00h SDIO Specification Version 1.00 01h SDIO Specification Version 1.10 02h SDIO Specification Version 1.20 (unreleased) 03h SDIO Specification Version 2.00 04h SDIO Specification Version 3.00 05h-0Fh Reserved for Future Use
fields.abstract: A read-only 4-bit field indicating the SDIO specification version supported by the card, with values ranging from 00h (Version 1.00) to 04h (Version 3.00), and values 05h-0Fh reserved for future use.

fields.name: SDx
fields.raw: SD Format Version Number These 4 bits contain the codes for the version of the Physical Layer Specification that this card supports. Value Physical Layer Specification 00h Physical Layer Specification Version 1.01 (March 2000) 01h Physical Layer Specification Version 1.10 (October 2004) 02h Physical Layer Specification Version 2.00 (May 2006) 03h Physical Layer Specification Version 3.0x 04h-0Fh Reserved for Future Use
fields.abstract: Read-only field indicating the SD card's Physical Layer Specification version, with values ranging from 00h (Version 1.01) to 03h (Version 3.0x), and 04h-0Fh reserved for future use.

fields.name: IOEx
fields.raw: Enable Function If this bit is reset to 0, the function is disabled. If this bit is set to 1, the function is enabled to start its initialization. The completion of initialization is indicated in IORx. On power up or after a reset, the card shall reset this bit to 0. The host can also use IOEx as a per function reset for error recovery. The host sequence for a per function reset is to reset IOEx to 0, wait until IORx becomes 0 and then set IOEx to 1 again. If the error is not recovered by this sequence, SDIO reset should be used noting that the operation of all functions will be aborted. Refer to Chapter 11 for relation to Master Power Control and Power Select.
fields.abstract: IOEx is a read-write enable bit that controls function initialization when set to 1, defaults to 0 on power-up/reset, and can be toggled by the host to perform per-function error recovery resets.

fields.name: IORx
fields.raw: I/O Function Ready If this bit is reset to 0, the function is not ready to operate. This may be caused by the function being disabled or not ready due to internal causes such as a built-in self-test in progress. If this bit is set to 1, the function is ready to operate. The functions shall set this bit to 1 within the timeout value defined in the TPLFE_ENABLE_TIMEOUT_VAL tuple. On power up or after a reset, this bit shall be set to 0. For any function that is not implemented on an SDIO card, this bit shall always be 0.
fields.abstract: Indicates whether the I/O function is ready to operate (1) or not ready due to being disabled, undergoing self-test, or other internal causes (0), with the bit defaulting to 0 on power-up or reset.

fields.name: IENx
fields.raw: Interrupt Enable for Function x If this bit is cleared to 0, any interrupt from this function shall not be sent to the host. If this bit is set to 1, then this function's interrupt shall be sent to the host if the master Interrupt Enable (bit 0) is also set to 1.
fields.abstract: Controls whether interrupts from function x are sent to the host when enabled, requiring both this bit and the master Interrupt Enable (bit 0) to be set for interrupt delivery.

fields.name: IENM
fields.raw: Interrupt Enable Master If this bit is cleared to 0, no interrupts from this card shall be sent to the host. If this bit is set to 1, then any function's interrupt shall be sent to the host.
fields.abstract: Controls the master interrupt enable for the card, where setting this bit allows any function's interrupt to be sent to the host while clearing it disables all interrupts from the card.

fields.name: INTx
fields.raw: Interrupt Pending for Function x If this bit is cleared to 0, this indicates that no interrupts are pending from this function. If this bit is set to 1, then this function has interrupt pending. Note that if the IENx or IENM bits are not set, the host cannot receive this pending interrupt. Addr: Field Type Description
fields.abstract: Indicates whether this function has an interrupt pending (1) or no interrupts pending (0), though the interrupt will only be delivered to the host if the corresponding enable bits (IENx or IENM) are set.

fields.name: ASx
fields.raw: Abort Select In order to abort an I/O read or write and free the SD bus, the function that is currently transferring data must be addressed. These 3 bits define which function's transfer to stop. For example, the abort the transfer to function number 3, the value of 03h would be written to these bits using CMD52 only. If the abort is addressed to a suspended function, it does not affect current data transaction. Note that this is an abort, not a reset. The addressed function shall return to the CMD state and data transfer pending to that function shall be halted. This abort procedure does not work for SPI write operations. To abort an SPI write data transfer use the STOP_TRAN token as defined in Section 7.3.3 of the Physical Layer Specification. This form of abort applies only to the functions of an SDIO card. For the memory of a combo card, the abort methods defined in the Physical Layer Specification shall be used to abort transfers to/from memory
fields.abstract: Selects which function (0-7) to abort its current I/O transfer and free the SD bus, written via CMD52 to stop a specific function's data transaction without affecting suspended functions.

fields.name: RES
fields.raw: I/O CARD RESET Setting the RES to 1 shall cause all I/O functions in an SDIO or Combo card to perform a soft reset. Setting the RES to 1 does not affect the current card protocol selection (SD vs. SPI mode) and CD Disable. Setting of the RES bit shall only be performed using CMD52. When RES=1, the values of AS2-0 are don't-cares. The RES bit is auto cleared, so there is no need to rewrite a value of 0. This bit is write-only, any read returns an undetermined value. Memory in a combo card is not affected.
fields.abstract: Write-only bit that triggers a soft reset of all I/O functions in an SDIO or Combo card when set to 1, auto-clears after execution, and does not affect card protocol selection or memory functions.

fields.name: Bus Width 1:0
fields.raw: Bus Width This field selects the bus width of the DAT line for a data transfer. All Full-Speed SDIO cards shall support both 1 and 4-bit bus widths. A Low-Speed SDIO card's support of 4-bit bus is optional. 1-bit bus width is the default. On reset or power-on these bits are cleared to 00. 8-bit bus mode can be supported only for an embedded device. 8-bit mode can be set if S8B is set to 0. 00b: 1-bit 01b: Reserved 10b: 4-bit bus 11b: 8-bit bus (only for embedded SDIO)
fields.abstract: Selects the DAT line bus width for data transfers, supporting 1-bit (default), 4-bit, or 8-bit (embedded devices only) modes.

fields.name: S8B
fields.raw: Support 8-bit Bus Mode This support bit is valid for embedded SDIO. SDIO card shall set this bit to 0. 0: 8-bit bus mode is not supported. 1: 8-bit bus mode is supported. (The details of 8-bit mode are not defined in this document but it will be defined in a future specification.)
fields.abstract: Indicates whether 8-bit bus mode is supported for embedded SDIO devices, where SDIO cards must set this bit to 0.

fields.name: ECSI
fields.raw: Enable Continuous SPI Interrupt If the SCSI bit is set, then this R/W bit is used to allow the SDIO card to assert the interrupt line in the SPI mode at any time, irrespective of the state of the CS line. This bit is cleared to zero on reset or power-up. If the SCSI bit is clear, this bit shall be read only and set to zero. This bit controls the assertion of interrupts in the SPI mode for all functions in the SDIO card.
fields.abstract: Enables the SDIO card to assert interrupts in SPI mode regardless of chip select (CS) line state, allowing continuous interrupt signaling when the SCSI capability bit is set.

fields.name: SCSI
fields.raw: Support Continuous SPI interrupt This read-only bit is set to indicate that this SDIO card supports the assertion of interrupts in the SPI mode at any time, irrespective of the status of the card select (CS) line. If this bit is zero, then this SDIO card can only assert the interrupt line in the SPI mode when the CS line is asserted. This bit signals the capability of all functions in the SDIO card. Addr: Field Type Description
fields.abstract: Read-only bit indicating whether the SDIO card supports continuous interrupt assertion in SPI mode regardless of chip select (CS) line status, or only when CS is asserted.

fields.name: CD Disable
fields.raw: Card Detect Disable Connect[0]/Disconnect[1] the 10K-90K ohm pull-up resistor on CD/DAT[3] (pin 1) of the card. The pull-up may be used for card detection. This bit is cleared to 0 on power-on (connected). Its state is not affected by a reset command. This bit shall be set to 1 before issuing CMD53.
fields.abstract: Controls the 10K-90K ohm pull-up resistor on the CD/DAT[3] pin, where 0 connects the resistor for card detection and 1 disconnects it (required before issuing CMD53).

fields.name: SDC
fields.raw: Support Direct Command (CMD52) Support bit of Direct Commands. This bit applies only to the SD modes, it does not apply to SPI mode. This flag bit reports the SDIO card's ability to execute CMD52 while data transfer is in progress. If this bit is set, all I/O functions shall accept and execute the CMD52 while data transfer is underway on the DAT[x] lines. Also, any memory in a combo card shall allow the CMD52 to execute while it is transferring data. Since the CMD52 does not use the DAT[x] lines, it is possible to execute while data transfer to a different address on the card is underway. CMD52 is described in 5.1. In SD or SPI mode, if an error occurs during data transfer the SDIO card shall accept a CMD52 to allow I/O abort and reset regardless of this bit value. If the card supports suspend/resume then it shall also support this bit.
fields.abstract: Indicates whether the SDIO card supports executing CMD52 (direct command) while a data transfer is in progress on the DAT[x] lines, applicable only to SD modes and not SPI mode.

fields.name: SMB
fields.raw: Support Multiple Block Transfer Support bit of Multi-Block transfer. This flag bit reports the SDIO card's ability to execute the IO_RW_EXTENDED command (CMD53) in the block mode. If this bit is set, all I/O functions (0-7) shall accept and execute CMD53 with the optional block mode bit set. The IO_RW_EXTENDED command is described in 5.3
fields.abstract: Indicates whether the SDIO card supports executing the IO_RW_EXTENDED command (CMD53) in block mode for multiple block transfers across all I/O functions (0-7).

fields.name: SRW
fields.raw: Support Read Wait Support bit of Read Wait control. This bit applies only to the SD modes, it does not apply to SPI mode. This flag bit reports the SDIO card's ability to support the Read Wait Control (RWC) operation. If set, all functions on the card are able to accept the wait signal on DAT[2]. RWC operation is described in Section 6.5. Any card that supports Suspend/Resume shall also support Read Wait
fields.abstract: Support bit indicating whether the SDIO card's functions can accept the Read Wait control signal on DAT[2], which is required for cards supporting Suspend/Resume operations.

fields.name: SBS
fields.raw: Support Bus Control Support bit of Suspend/Resume. This bit applies only to the SD modes, it does not apply to SPI mode. This flag bit reports the SDIO card's ability to Suspend and Resume operations at the request of the host. If this bit is set, all functions except 0 shall accept a request to suspend operations and resume under host control. Suspend/Resume operation is described in Section 6.4. If this bit is 0, registers (0Ch-0Fh) shall not be supported.
fields.abstract: Reports whether the SDIO card supports host-controlled Suspend/Resume operations for all non-zero functions in SD modes, with support indicated when set and registers 0Ch-0Fh only valid when this capability is present.

fields.name: S4MI
fields.raw: Support Block Gap Interrupt Support bit of interrupt between blocks of data in 4-bit SD mode. This flag bit reports the SDIO card's ability to generate interrupts during a 4-bit multi-block data transfer. If this bit is 0, then the SDIO card is not able to signal an interrupt during a multi-block data transfer in 4-bit mode. In this case, the interrupt is not signaled until after the data transfer is complete. If this bit is 1, then the SDIO card is able to signal an interrupt between blocks while data transfer is in progress. This operation is described in 8.1.4 Note, even if a card does not support the interrupt during 4-bit block transfer (S4MI=0), the card may signal interrupts during all other Interrupt Periods while the interrupt is enabled (IENx=1). Addr: Field Type Description
fields.abstract: Read-only bit indicating whether the SDIO card supports signaling interrupts between blocks during 4-bit multi-block data transfers, where 0 means interrupts are deferred until transfer completion and 1 means inter-block interrupt signaling is supported.

fields.name: E4MI
fields.raw: Enable Block Gap Interrupt Enable bit of interrupt between blocks of data in 4-bit SD mode. Enable the multi-block IRQ during 4-bit transfer for the SDIO card. When this bit is 0, the card shall not signal interrupts during a 4-bit multi-block data transfer. If this bit is 1, the card shall generate interrupts during 4 bit multi-block data transfers as described in 8.1.4 If this SDIO card does not support 4 bit multi-block IRQs (S4MI=0), then this bit shall be R/O and always read as 0. This bit shall be cleared to 0 by any reset. When operating more than 25MB/sec data rate in SDR50, SDR104 or DDR50, Block Gap Interrupt shall not be used (this bit is set to 0). It is difficult for a host to use the narrow interrupt period considering propagation delay from card to host.
fields.abstract: Enable Block Gap Interrupt for 4-bit SD mode, allowing SDIO cards to signal interrupts during 4-bit multi-block data transfers when set to 1, or suppressing such interrupts when set to 0.

fields.name: LSC
fields.raw: Low-Speed Card If this bit is set, it indicates that the SDIO card is a Low-Speed card (Refer to Section 2.1). If this bit is clear, the SDIO card is a Full-Speed card.
fields.abstract: Indicates whether the SDIO card is a Low-Speed card (bit set) or a Full-Speed card (bit clear).

fields.name: 4BLS
fields.raw: 4-bit Mode Support for Low-Speed Card If the SDIO card is a Low-Speed card (LSC=1) and it supports 4-bit data transfer, then this bit shall be set. If the card is not Low-Speed or if the card does not support 4-bit transfer, then this bit shall be zero. 09h-
fields.abstract: Indicates whether a Low-Speed SDIO card supports 4-bit data transfer mode, valid only when the card is identified as Low-Speed (LSC=1).

fields.name: Pointer to card's common CIS
fields.raw: Common CIS Pointer This 3-byte pointer points to the start of the card's common CIS. The common CIS contains information relation to the entire card. The card common CIS shall be located within the CIS space of function 0 (001000h- 017FFFh) as described in Section 6.11. A card common CIS is mandatory for all SDIO cards. This pointer is stored in little-endian format (LSB first).
fields.abstract: A 3-byte little-endian read-only pointer indicating the starting address of the card's mandatory common Card Information Structure (CIS) within function 0's CIS space.

fields.name: BS
fields.raw: Bus Status If this bit is set to 1, then the currently addressed function (selected by FSx or by the function number in an I/O command) is currently executing a command which transfers data on the DAT[x] line(s). If this bit is 0, then the addressed function is not using the data bus. This bit is used by the host to determine which function of a multi-function or combo card is currently performing data transfer. Note that this bit is a part of the optional Suspend/Resume protocol. If the card does not support Suspend/Resume, this bit shall be read as 0. Any access to the CIA may not be suspended, so in this case, BS shall always be set to 1, irrespective of the host setting BR to 1. Addr: Field Type Description
fields.abstract: The BS (Bus Status) field is a read-only bit that indicates whether the currently addressed function is actively executing a command that transfers data on the DAT line(s), used by the host to identify which function in a multi-function or combo card is performing data transfer as part of the optional Suspend/Resume protocol.

fields.name: BR
fields.raw: Bus Release Request This bit is used to request that the addressed function (selected by FSx or by the function number in CMD53 or Memory commands using DAT line) release the Data lines and suspend operation. If the host sets this bit to 1, the addressed function shall temporarily halt data transfer on the DAT[x] lines and suspend the command that is in process. The BR bit shall remain set to 1 until the release is complete. If the card can never accept the suspend request while executing transactions, the card shall return response with BR cleared to 0 and BS set to 1. This indicates that the suspend request is cancelled by the card and thus the host should not issue a cancel suspend command. The followings are the cases where the card can cancel a suspend request: Transaction addressed to function 0. The card knows the transfer will terminate soon. The card knows the transfer is timing critical (i.e. If suspended, the transfer cannot proceed). A Multi function card that indicates SBS=1, but contains a function that does not support suspend/resume. Once the function is in suspend, it shall signal the host by clearing the BS and BR bits. The host can monitor the status of the suspend request by reading the BR bit. If it is set, the suspend request is still in progress. A pending suspend request can be cancelled by the host by writing 0 to the BR bit. The Standard Host Specification defines following suspend sequence: If the suspend request is not accepted, the host retries with a cancel suspend request command. Even if the card received a cancel suspend command, it should accept suspend if possible. If the card does not accept suspend, the host considers the function to have never suspend. However, the host should monitor the BR, BS and EXx bits to confirm that the suspend request was cancelled. If SBS=0, this bit shall be R/O and read as 0.
fields.abstract: Request for the addressed function to release the Data lines and suspend its current operation, remaining set until the release is complete.

fields.name: FSx
fields.raw: Select Function These four bits are used to select a function number (0-7) or the memory of a combo card (8) for Suspend/Resume. There are two methods to write the value of FSx. First, an I/O write to the register in the CCCR and second, a new I/O command that causes the FSx to be set to the function number in that command. The value of FSx shall remain until overwritten. If a function or memory is currently suspended, the writing of its number to FSx shall re-start (resume) the data transfer operation When reading FSx, the value returned shall be the number of the currently addressed function. Note that when reading FSx, if the Bus Status is 0 (BS=0), the FSx value is undefined. The FSx bits are coded as follows: FSx Current Transaction Transaction of function 0 (CIA) 0001-0111 Transaction to functions 1-7 Transaction of memory in combo card 1001-1111 Not defined, reserved for future use If SBS=0 these bits shall be R/O. Addr: Field Type Description
fields.abstract: Selects a function number (0-7) or combo card memory (8) for Suspend/Resume operations, with the value persisting until overwritten and triggering resume if the selected function is currently suspended.

fields.name: DF
fields.raw: Data Flag A data transaction is resumed by writing its number to FSx. Once the transaction is resumed, the DF indicates if more data will be transferred. If DF is cleared to 0, then no additional data will be transferred after the function or memory is resumed. If DF is set to 1, then there is more data to transfer that will begin after the function or memory in resumed. The DF flag can be used to control the interrupt cycle in 4-bit mode. If DF=1, there is more data to transfer after restoring the function. In this case, the interrupt cycle should be disabled. If DF=0, the function or memory was suspended at end of data transfer (during busy). In this case, no data transfer shall begin after resume so the host can detect a start interrupt cycle after restore. When resuming, if the suspended function cannot continue data transfer the card shall return DF=0 to abort the transfer.
fields.abstract: The Data Flag (DF) is a read-only indicator that signals whether additional data remains to be transferred after a suspended transaction is resumed, useful for controlling interrupt cycles in 4-bit mode.

fields.name: EXx
fields.raw: Execution Flag These 8 bits are used by the host to determine the current execution status of all functions (1-7) and memory (0). The bit is set to 1 for each function or memory that is currently executing a command. The EXx bits tell the host that a function or memory is currently executing a command so no additional command should be issued to that function/memory. These bits are only defined if SBS=1. This bit is set if the function is active. If SBS=0 these bits shall be read as zero.
fields.abstract: Read-only execution flags indicating which functions (1-7) and memory (0) are currently executing commands, with each bit set to 1 when the corresponding function/memory is busy; only valid when SBS=1, otherwise reads as zero.

fields.name: RFx
fields.raw: Ready Flag These 8 bits tell the host the read or write busy status for functions (1-7) and memory (0). If a function or memory is executing a write transaction, an RFx bit cleared to 0 indicates the function/memory is busy and not ready to accept more data. If the RFx bit is set to 1, then the function/memory can accept write data. If a function/memory is executing a read command, if the RFx bit is cleared to 0, it indicates that read data is NOT available. If the bit is set to 1, it indicates that read data is ready to be transferred. These bits are only defined if SBS=1. Setting a bit to 1 indicates the function is ready to accept the resume command. There are two conditions where the function will set the bit to 1. One is when the function (executing or suspended) is ready to continue data transfer. The second is when the suspended function cannot continue data transfer. If SBS=0 these bits shall be read as zero. 10h-
fields.abstract: An 8-bit read-only status field indicating the ready/busy state for functions 1-7 and memory (function 0), where a set bit indicates the function/memory is ready to accept write data or has read data available, and a cleared bit indicates busy or data not available.

fields.name: FN0 Block Size
fields.raw: Block Size for Function 0 This 16-bit register sets the block size for I/O block operations for Function 0 only. If this card does not support I/O block operations (SMB=0), then this register becomes read-only and shall always read 0000h. The maximum block size is 2048 (0800h) and the minimum is 1. At power-up or reset, this register shall be initially loaded with a value of 0000h. The host is responsible for setting the appropriate value for the block size supported by function 0. This pointer is stored in little-endian format (LSB first).
fields.abstract: Block Size for Function 0 sets the 16-bit block size (1-2048 bytes) for I/O block operations on Function 0, initializing to 0000h at power-up and becoming read-only (returning 0000h) if block operations are not supported.

fields.name: SMPC
fields.raw: Support Master Power Control These bits tell the host if the card supports Master Power Control. SMPC=0: The total card power is up to 720mW (3.6Vx200mA), even if all functions are active (IOEx=1). EMPC, SPS and EPS shall be zero. SMPC=1: The total card power may exceed 720mW (3.6Vx200mA). Controls of EMPC, SPS and EPS are available. Addr: Field Type Description
fields.abstract: Indicates whether the card supports Master Power Control, where 0 means total card power stays within 720mW and 1 means power may exceed 720mW with EMPC, SPS, and EPS controls available.

fields.name: EMPC
fields.raw: Enable Master Power Control EMPC=0 (default): The total card power shall be up to 720mW (3.6Vx 200mA). The card automatically switches the mode of function(s) to lower current or does not allow some functions to become enabled, regardless of the value of EPS, so that total card power is 720mW or less. (The card manufacturer determines which functions operate and their modes to guarantee this limit.) EMPC=1: The total card power may exceed 720mW and SPS and EPS are available. The host uses SPS, EPS in FBR and IOEx to enable higher current function modes based on the host's ability to supply the necessary current. If PS[3:0]=0 (Ver1.10 compatible), two power modes can be selected by using SPS, EPS in FBR for an SDIO Card supporting 2.7V-3.6V Power supply range. PS[3:0] >0 is defined by Ver3.00 Power Control Extension (Applicable to multiple voltages device).
fields.abstract: Enable Master Power Control bit that determines whether total card power is limited to 720mW (EMPC=0) or may exceed 720mW with SPS and EPS power control features available (EMPC=1).

fields.name: SHS
fields.raw: Support High-Speed This flag bit reports the card's ability to operate in High-Speed mode SHS=0: The card does not support High-Speed mode SHS=1: The card supports High-Speed mode. The host enables High-Speed mode via the EHS bit. Refer to Chapter 12 for details on switching between default and High-Speed mode.
fields.abstract: Read-only flag indicating whether the card supports High-Speed mode operation, which can be enabled by the host via the EHS bit when supported.

fields.name: BSSx
fields.raw: Bus Speed Select This field is used to select bus speed mode. This field shall be set by CMD52 and the new bus speed mode is changed within 8 clock cycles after the response of CMD52. Refer to Section 12 for details on switching between default and High-Speed mode. If the card is initialized in 3.3V signaling, then BSS0 is effective. When SHS is set to 0, writing to this bit is ignored and always indicates 0. The card operates in High-Speed timing mode with a clock rate up to 50MHz. BSS[2:0] Bus Speed 3.3V Max. Clock Frequency xx0b: Default Speed 25MHz xx1b: High Speed 50MHz If the card is initialized in 1.8V signaling, then BSS[2:0] is effective. A card that supports UHS-I shall support High Speed mode and SHS shall be set to 1. One of the UHS-I modes is selected as follows. BSS[2:0] Bus Speed 1.8V Max Clock Frequency 000b: SDR12 25MHz 001b: SDR25 50MHz 010b: SDR50 100MHz 011b: SDR104 208MHz 100b: DDR50 50MHz 101b-111b: Reserved
fields.abstract: Selects the SDIO bus speed mode, which takes effect within 8 clock cycles after CMD52 response, with BSS0 effective for 3.3V signaling and High-Speed mode supporting clock rates up to 50MHz when enabled.

fields.name: SSDR50
fields.raw: Support SDR50 This bit indicates support of SDR50. If this bit is set to 1, SDR12 and SDR25 shall be supported. High Speed mode in 3.3V signaling also shall be supported. Support bit of SDR50 0b: SDR50 is not supported 1b: SDR50 is supported Addr: Field Type Description
fields.abstract: This read-only bit indicates whether SDR50 mode is supported, where support also implies SDR12, SDR25, and High Speed mode at 3.3V signaling are available.

fields.name: SSDR104
fields.raw: Support SDR104 This bit indicates support of SDR104. If this bit is set to 1, SDR12, SDR25 and SDR50 shall be supported. High Speed mode in 3.3V signaling also shall be supported. Support bit of SDR104 0b: SDR104 is not supported 1b: SDR104 is supported
fields.abstract: Indicates whether SDR104 mode is supported, which when enabled also implies support for SDR12, SDR25, SDR50, and High Speed mode at 3.3V signaling.

fields.name: SDDR50
fields.raw: Support DDR50 This bit indicates support of DDR50. If this bit is set to 1, SDR12, SDR25 and SDR50 shall be supported. High Speed mode in 3.3V signaling also shall be supported. Support bit of DDR50 0b: DDR50 is not supported 1b: DDR50 is supported
fields.abstract: Indicates whether DDR50 mode is supported, which when enabled also implies support for SDR12, SDR25, SDR50, and High Speed mode in 3.3V signaling.

fields.name: SDTA
fields.raw: Support Driver Type A This bit indicates support of Driver Type A. Support bit of Driver Type A 0b: Driver Type A is not supported 1b: Driver Type A is supported
fields.abstract: Read-only bit indicating whether Driver Type A is supported by the hardware.

fields.name: SDTC
fields.raw: Support Driver Type C This bit indicates support of Driver Type C. Support bit of Driver Type C 0b: Driver Type C is not supported 1b: Driver Type C is supported
fields.abstract: Indicates whether Driver Type C is supported by the hardware (read-only status bit).

fields.name: SDTD
fields.raw: Support Driver Type D This bit indicates support of Driver Type D. Support bit of Driver Type D 0b: Driver Type D is not supported 1b: Driver Type D is supported
fields.abstract: Indicates whether Driver Type D is supported by the host controller.

fields.name: DTSx
fields.raw: Driver Type Select This 2-bit field is used to select driver type. Type B is defined as the default driver strength. If unsupported driver type is selected, Type B is selected. Refer to the Physical Layer Specification Version 3.0x for more detail. DTS[1:0] Driver Type Selected 00b: Type B 01b: Type A (SDTA=1) or Type B (SDTA=0) 10b: Type C (SDTC=1) or Type B (SDTC=0) 11b: Type D (SDTD=1) or Type B (SDTD=0)
fields.abstract: Selects the SD card driver type (A, B, C, or D) for signal strength control, defaulting to Type B if the selected type is unsupported.

fields.name: SAI
fields.raw: Support Asynchronous Interrupt Support bit of Asynchronous Interrupt. If the card supports asynchronous interrupt in SD 4-bit mode (interrupt can be asserted without SD clock during specified period), this bit is set to 1. Addr: Field Type Description
fields.abstract: Indicates whether the card supports asynchronous interrupt capability in SD 4-bit mode, allowing interrupt assertion without the SD clock during specified periods.

fields.name: EAI
fields.raw: Enable Asynchronous Interrupt Enable bit of Asynchronous Interrupt. When SAI is set to 0, writing to this bit is ignored and always indicates 0. This bit is effective in SD 4-bit mode. EAI Interrupt Mode 0b: Asynchronous Interrupt is disabled 1b: Asynchronous Interrupt is enabled RFU R/O Any bit defined as Reserved for Future Use (RFU) shall be read-only and shall be read as 0. Reserved for Vendors R/W These 16 registers are reserved for the manufacturer of the I/O card to be used for any operations that are defined by and specific to any vendor unique operation. Information about the use of these optional registers needs to be obtained from the SDIO card maker. Reading and/or writing these registers without understanding the vendor's definitions may cause unexpected behavior or even damage to the card. Table 6-2 : CCCR bit Definitions
fields.abstract: Enable Asynchronous Interrupt (EAI) bit that enables or disables asynchronous interrupt functionality in SD 4-bit mode, effective only when SAI (asynchronous interrupt support) is available.

fields.name: SDIO Standard Function Interface Code
fields.raw: The SDIO Standard Function code identifies those I/O functions which implement the recommended standard interface as defined in a separate Application Specification. Codes: 0h: No SDIO standard interface supported; 1h: SDIO Standard UART; 2h: SDIO Bluetooth Type-A; 3h: SDIO Bluetooth Type-B; 4h: GPS; 5h: Camera; 6h: PHS; 7h: WLAN; 8h-Eh: Reserved; Fh: Check Extended code in n01h
fields.abstract: Read-only field that identifies the SDIO standard function interface type implemented by the I/O function, with codes ranging from 0h (none) to Fh (extended code), including UART, Bluetooth, GPS, Camera, PHS, and WLAN interfaces.

fields.name: Function Supports CSA
fields.raw: If this function supports and contains a Code Storage Area (CSA) this bit shall be set to 1. If this function does not support a CSA this bit shall be cleared to 0. CSA enable is controlled by bit 7 of register n00h.
fields.abstract: Indicates whether this function supports and contains a Code Storage Area (CSA), with CSA enable controlled by bit 7 of register n00h.

fields.name: Function CSA Enable
fields.raw: This bit controls access to the Code Storage Area for this function. If cleared to 0 any read or write access to the CSA shall be blocked. If set to 1 access to the CSA is allowed. Cleared to 0 upon reset. If function does not support CSA (0n00h bit 6=0) then this bit shall be R/O and always read as 0.
fields.abstract: Controls access to the Code Storage Area (CSA) for this function; when cleared, all CSA read/write access is blocked, and when set, CSA access is permitted.

fields.name: Extended SDIO Standard Function interface code
fields.raw: This is the extension of the SDIO Standard Function interface code. If the SDIO Standard Function interface code is greater than Eh then this byte shall contain the code and the standard code (100h bits 3-0) shall contain a value of Fh. If the standard code is less than Fh then this byte shall be 00h.
fields.abstract: Extended interface code for SDIO Standard Function, used when the standard 4-bit interface code field contains Fh to indicate the actual code is stored in this extended byte.

fields.name: SPS
fields.raw: Support Power Selection. This bit indicates if the function has Power Selection. SPS=0: This function has no Power Selection; EPS shall be zero. SPS=1: This function has 2 power modes which are selected by EPS. This bit is effective when EMPC=1 in CCCR and PS[3:0]=0.
fields.abstract: Indicates whether the function supports power selection between two power modes (when set) or has no power selection capability (when cleared), effective only when EMPC=1 in CCCR and PS[3:0]=0.

fields.name: EPS
fields.raw: Enable Power Selection. EPS=0 (default): The function operates in Higher Current Mode; maximum current given in TPLFE_HP_MAX_PWR_3.3V. EPS=1: The function works in Lower Current Mode; maximum current given in TPLFE_LP_MAX_PWR_3.3V. This bit shall be reset when IOEx=0. Effective when EMPC=1 in CCCR and PS[3:0]=0.
fields.abstract: Enable Power Selection bit that switches the function between Higher Current Mode (EPS=0, using HP_MAX_PWR) and Lower Current Mode (EPS=1, using LP_MAX_PWR), effective only when EMPC=1 and PS[3:0]=0, and automatically reset when IOEx=0.

fields.name: PSx
fields.raw: Power State PS[3:0]. If PS[3:0] is set to 0 TPL_CODE CISTPL_FUNCE (22h) extension 01h is used and the card power is controlled by EMPC and EPS (SDIO Version 2.00 Compatible Mode). If non-zero the card power state is specified in the PS table defined in CISTPL_FUNCE extension 04h.
fields.abstract: Power State field that controls card power mode, where 0 uses SDIO 2.00 compatible EMPC/EPS control via CISTPL_FUNCE extension 01h, and non-zero values specify power states defined in the CISTPL_FUNCE extension 04h PS table.

fields.name: Function 1-7 I/O Block Size
fields.raw: This 16-bit register sets the block size for I/O block operations for each function (1-7). If block operations not supported (SMB=0) this register is read-only and reads 0000h. Maximum block size is 2048 (0800h) minimum is 1 (0001h). At power-up or reset initially loaded with 0000h. Host responsible for setting appropriate value. Stored in little-endian format (LSB first).
fields.abstract: A 16-bit read-write register that configures the block size (1-2048 bytes) for I/O block operations on SDIO functions 1-7, initialized to 0000h at reset and stored in little-endian format, or read-only returning 0000h if block operations are unsupported.
